jp: 友達[ともだち]「昨日[きのう]、初[はじ]めてマラソンを走[はし]ったんだ。」私[わたし]「{それ|ko-context}はすごいね。」。
en: Friend: "Yesterday I ran a marathon for the first time." Me: "That's amazing."
why: The speaker reacts to what the friend has just said, so the thing is それ.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん「膝[ひざ]を痛[いた]めて、しばらく走[はし]れません。」私[わたし]「{それ|ko-context}は心配[しんぱい]ですね。お大事[だいじ]に。」。
en: Ms. Yamada: "I hurt my knee and can't run for a while." Me: "That's worrying. Take care."
why: The speaker picks up what the other person has just said, so it is それ.

jp: 母[はは]「ねえ、{あれ|ko-context}、まだ持[も]ってる？去年[きょねん]、家族[かぞく]で山[やま]に登[のぼ]ったときに拾[ひろ]った石[いし]。」。
en: Mother: "Hey, do you still have that thing? The stone we picked up when we climbed the mountain as a family last year."
why: Both people remember the stone from shared experience and it has not been mentioned yet, so it is あれ.

jp: 友達[ともだち]「来週[らいしゅう]の試合[しあい]、雨[あめ]で中止[ちゅうし]になるかもしれないって。」私[わたし]「えっ、{それ|ko-context}本当[ほんとう]？」。
en: Friend: "They say next week's match may be cancelled because of rain." Me: "What? Is that true?"
why: The speaker asks about what the friend has just said, so it is それ.

jp: {あれ|ko-context}はもう一度[いちど]見[み]たいね。去年[きょねん]の夏[なつ]、二人[ふたり]で山[やま]の上[うえ]から見[み]た星空[ほしぞら]。
en: I'd like to see that once more. The starry sky the two of us saw from the mountaintop last summer.
why: A shared memory that has not just been mentioned by the listener is referred to with あれ.

jp: 医者[いしゃ]「毎日[まいにち]三十分[さんじゅっぷん]歩[ある]くと、体[からだ]にいいですよ。」患者[かんじゃ]「{それ|ko-context}なら、続[つづ]けられそうです。」。
en: Doctor: "Walking thirty minutes every day is good for your body." Patient: "If that's all, I think I can keep it up."
why: The patient responds to the doctor's advice just given, so it is それ (それなら = if that's the case).

jp: ねえ、{あれ|ko-context}どうなった？先週[せんしゅう]、二人[ふたり]で相談[そうだん]した、ジムに入[はい]る話[はなし]。
en: Hey, what happened with that? The thing about joining a gym that we talked over together last week.
why: Both speakers know the matter from an earlier talk and it has not been raised in this conversation, so it is あれ.
